q: What does a red octagonal sign mean?
explanation: Red octagon = full stop behind the line.

q: An inverted (point-down) triangle sign means…
explanation: Inverted triangle = yield. Slow down, stop only if needed.

q: A yellow diamond sign is…
explanation: Yellow diamond signs warn of upcoming conditions.

q: Solid white line between lanes means…
explanation: Solid white = lane change discouraged; cross only when needed.

q: Solid yellow line on your side means…
explanation: Solid yellow on your side = no passing.

q: Green guide signs indicate…
explanation: Green signs guide drivers — directions, exits, mileage.

q: Flashing yellow signal means…
explanation: Flashing yellow = proceed with caution.

q: Flashing red signal means…
explanation: Flashing red is treated as a stop sign.

q: Two cars arrive at a 4-way stop together. Who goes first?
explanation: At a 4-way stop, the car on the right has right-of-way.

q: Turning left at a green (no arrow), you yield to…
explanation: Green ball = permissive; yield to oncoming traffic AND pedestrians.

q: Emergency vehicle with lights and sirens approaches. You…
explanation: Pull to the right edge of the road and stop.

q: Entering a roundabout, you must…
options: Yield to traffic in the circle
explanation: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.

q: School bus stopped with flashing red lights on undivided road…
explanation: Both directions must stop on an undivided road.

q: Right turn on red is permitted unless…
options: A sign prohibits it or red arrow shown
explanation: Right on red is legal after a full stop unless prohibited (NYC is the major exception — banned by default).

q: Federal commercial driver BAC limit is…
explanation: Commercial drivers: 0.04% federal limit, uniform in all states.

q: Open container in the passenger area is…
explanation: Open containers are prohibited in nearly every state under federal incentive law (23 USC 154).

q: Safe following distance rule…
explanation: Use the 3-second rule; extend to 4+ seconds in rain/snow.

q: Left lane on a multi-lane highway is for…
explanation: Keep right except to pass — codified in most state vehicle codes.

q: School/work zone fines are typically…
explanation: School/work zone fines are doubled in most states.

q: Basic speed law means…
options: No faster than safe for conditions
explanation: Drive no faster than is safe for current conditions, even below the posted limit.

q: If you skid on a wet road, you should…
options: Steer into skid, ease off gas
explanation: Steer where you want to go and ease off the gas.

q: Hydroplaning can start around…
explanation: Hydroplaning can start near 35 mph on wet roads with worn tires.

q: Merging onto a freeway you should…
options: Match traffic speed and merge in a gap
explanation: Match the speed of freeway traffic and merge smoothly.

q: A pedestrian at a marked crosswalk has…
options: Right of way only at lights
Right of way at night only
explanation: Pedestrians in crosswalks have right of way in every state.

q: When parking on a hill facing downhill with a curb…
explanation: Downhill with curb: turn wheels into the curb (right).

q: When parking on a hill facing uphill with a curb…
explanation: Uphill with curb: turn wheels away from the curb (left).

q: Driving in fog you should use…
explanation: Low beams/fog lights; high beams glare back off the fog.

q: ABS brakes during emergency stop — you should…
explanation: With ABS, press and hold firmly; the system pulses for you.

q: A double solid yellow line means…
explanation: Double solid yellow = no passing either direction.

q: Headlights are required from…
explanation: Headlights required from sunset to sunrise and in low visibility (typical state code: ½ hour after sunset to ½ hour before sunrise).

q: When following a motorcycle you should…
explanation: Motorcycles can stop faster — allow extra following distance (4-second rule).

q: Texting while driving is…
explanation: Texting while driving is illegal in 48 states + DC (Missouri and Montana are the lone partial exceptions).

q: A flashing yellow arrow for left turn means…
options: Turn allowed but yield to oncoming
explanation: Flashing yellow arrow = turn permitted, yield to oncoming traffic.

q: On a 4-lane divided highway, school bus stops with flashing reds. Oncoming traffic must…
explanation: On a divided highway with a physical median, oncoming traffic does NOT need to stop.

q: If your tire blows out you should…
options: Grip wheel, ease off gas, coast to side
explanation: Grip the wheel firmly, ease off the gas, coast to slow down before braking gently.

q: Move Over laws require you to…
options: Speed up past stopped emergency vehicles
Change lanes away or slow down
explanation: Move Over: change lanes away from stopped emergency/utility/tow vehicles, or slow significantly. Now law in all 50 states.

q: A solid green arrow means…
options: Protected turn — yield to nothing in your path
explanation: Solid green arrow = protected turn; oncoming traffic is stopped.

q: Cannabis affects driving by…
explanation: THC slows reaction time and impairs judgment of speed/distance. DUI applies in every state regardless of recreational legality.

q: Three-point turn (K-turn) requires you to check…
explanation: Always check both directions and mirrors before each move.

q: Pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog has…
explanation: Every state code grants absolute right of way to a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog.

q: When passing a bicyclist most states require at least…
explanation: 3-foot passing law is on the books in 33+ states; the remainder require 'safe distance'.

q: Backing up safely you should…
options: Turn your head and look back
explanation: Always turn your head and look — camera/mirrors have blind spots.

q: Yellow traffic light means…
options: Stop if you can do so safely
explanation: Yellow = stop if you can do so safely; do NOT accelerate to beat it.

q: First-offense DUI typically includes…
options: Fines, suspension, possible jail, mandatory education
explanation: Even a first DUI involves fines, license suspension, possible jail, and mandatory alcohol education in every state.

q: Liver metabolizes about one standard drink per…
explanation: ~1 drink per hour. Coffee, food, and cold showers do NOT speed this up.

q: Highway hypnosis is best avoided by…
explanation: Take a break every 2 hours; keep eyes scanning, not fixed.

q: Roundabout: when do you signal?
explanation: Signal right just before your exit so others know you're leaving.

q: Driving with worn tire tread is dangerous because…
options: Loss of traction, longer stops, hydroplane risk
explanation: Worn tread loses traction, lengthens stops, raises hydroplane risk. Legal minimum: 2/32 inch.

q: Sharing the road with large trucks — best practice…
options: Cut in front close after passing
explanation: Trucks have large No-Zones (blind spots) on all four sides; avoid lingering beside them.

q: Driving on wet leaves is similar to driving on…
explanation: Wet leaves act like ice — reduce speed and avoid sudden moves.

q: Seat belts are required for…
options: All occupants in nearly every state
explanation: All 50 states require driver belts; 49 states require front-seat passenger belts (NH is the only exception for adults).

q: A red flashing arrow means…
explanation: Red flashing arrow is treated like a stop sign for that turning movement.

q: Drowsy driving is most comparable to…
explanation: Being awake 18+ hours impairs you like a 0.05% BAC; 24 hours = 0.10%.

q: If your brakes fail you should…
options: Pump brakes, downshift, then parking brake gradually
explanation: Pump pedal, downshift to slow via engine, then apply parking brake gradually.

q: An octagonal red sign in any color/shape configuration always means…
explanation: Shape alone signals STOP — recognizable even when snow-covered.
